<!DOCTYPE html>
<!--
================================================================================
  FILE:   Babor — SO Entry (pricing-rule capture)
  PATH:   Custom/Babor/Babor_SO_Entry.htm
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  A Sales Order entry screen that records WHICH PRICING RULE produced each
  line's price.

  Why this exists: `soitem` stores only the resulting unitPrice. Several of
  this client's rules resolve to the SAME price for DIFFERENT reasons
  (distributor samples, media giveaways, free bags, Business Development
  Fund are all separate 100%-off rules), so the applied rule cannot be
  recovered by inference afterwards — and the desktop client displays which
  rule COULD have produced a price, not the one the operator chose. Without
  a record of the reason there is no "what did we give away, and why"
  report. This screen captures the reason at entry time into an soitem
  custom field, which Babor_Pricing_Rule_Sales.htm then reports on.

  Design constraints that shaped it:
    * The operator will not accept extra clicks. Today she hunts the rule in
      a modal, per line. Here the rule is one cell in the grid, pre-filled
      from the customer's note, and reachable by keyboard.
    * One order legitimately mixes many reasons across its lines, so the
      rule is per LINE, never per order.

  KNOWN LIMITATION: only the rule NAME is stored, so renaming a pricing rule
  orphans the history written before the rename. The fix is a second
  "Pricing Rule Id" custom field; deliberately not built.

  CREATE-ONLY. The REST API has no update-an-existing-SO endpoint, so this
  screen cannot edit an order once written. Status defaults to Estimate.

  Requires: the SO_PRICE_OVERRIDE access right (setting a line unitPrice is
  gated), and an soitem custom field named in Settings (default
  "Pricing Rule").
================================================================================
-->
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
    <title>Sales Order Entry — Fishbowl BI</title>

    <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@300;400;500;600;700;800&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">

    <!-- Shared Fishbowl BI lib — inlined by Fishbowl from the saved script.
         Source of truth: scripts/fb-lib.js. Included exactly ONCE. -->
    <script>
        {% Script fb-lib %}
    </script>

    <!-- Shared stylesheet — source of truth: scripts/fb-styles.css. Must come
         before the local block so local rules win on identical selectors. -->
    <style>
        {% Style fb-styles %}
    </style>

    <style>
        * { box-sizing: border-box; }
        html, body { margin: 0; padding: 0; height: 100%; }
        body {
            font-family: 'Inter', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif;
            font-size: 13px; color: var(--c-primary); background: var(--bg-1);
            display: flex; flex-direction: column; min-height: 100vh;
            padding-bottom: var(--debug-drawer-h, 0px);
            transition: padding-bottom 0.12s ease;
        }
        header h1 { font-size: 16px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--c-primary); margin: 0; line-height: 1.15; }
        #statusLine { font-size: 12px; color: var(--c-tertiary); line-height: 1.15; margin: 2px 0 0; }
        .hdr-actions { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; }
        .hdr-sep { width: 1px; height: 18px; background: var(--border); margin: 0 4px; }

        /* =====================================================
           APP SHELL — order header, then a grid that eats the rest
           ===================================================== */
        .app-shell {
            flex: 1 1 auto; display: flex; flex-direction: column; min-height: 0;
            padding: 12px 16px; gap: 10px;
            /* The shell scrolls when its contents cannot fit the viewport.
               Without this the order header is unreachable on a short screen,
               because the grid below it absorbs every spare pixel. */
            overflow-y: auto;
        }

        .card {
            background: var(--bg-primary); border: 1px solid var(--border);
            border-radius: var(--r-card); box-shadow: var(--sh1);
        }

        /* ── ORDER HEADER ─────────────────────────────────────
           Collapses to a one-line summary so the line grid owns the
           vertical space. The desktop client uses tabs; in a single pane a
           collapse is the honest equivalent. */
        .oh-head {
            display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px;
            padding: 8px 12px; cursor: pointer; user-select: none;
        }
        .oh-caret { font-size: 11px; color: var(--c-tertiary); transition: transform .15s; }
        .oh-head.collapsed .oh-caret { transform: rotate(-90deg); }
        .oh-title { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: .02em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--c-secondary); }
        .oh-summary { font-size: 12px; color: var(--c-secondary); flex: 1; min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; }
        .oh-body { padding: 4px 12px 12px; border-top: 1px solid var(--border); }
        .oh-body.hidden { display: none; }
        .oh-grid {
            display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(190px, 1fr));
            gap: 10px 14px; align-items: start;
        }
        .fld { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 3px; min-width: 0; }
        .fld label { font-size: 10px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: .04em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--c-tertiary); }
        .fld label .req { color: var(--fb-negative); }
        .fld input, .fld select, .fld textarea {
            font-family: inherit; font-size: 12.5px; color: var(--c-primary);
            padding: 6px 8px; border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); border-radius: var(--r-btn);
            background: #fff; width: 100%; min-width: 0;
        }
        .fld input:focus, .fld select:focus, .fld textarea:focus {
            outline: none; border-color: var(--fb-blue); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(45,156,219,.15);
        }
        .fld .ro { background: var(--bg-2); color: var(--c-secondary); }
        .fb-field textarea {
            width: 100%; font-family: var(--mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 11.5px;
            padding: 6px 8px; border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); border-radius: var(--r-btn);
            background: #fff; resize: vertical; line-height: 1.5;
        }
        .fb-field textarea:focus { outline: none; border-color: var(--fb-blue); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(45,156,219,.15); }
        .with-btn { display: flex; gap: 4px; align-items: stretch; min-width: 0; }
        .with-btn input { flex: 1; min-width: 0; }
        .mini-btn {
            flex: 0 0 auto; width: 30px; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1; cursor: pointer;
            border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); border-radius: var(--r-btn);
            background: #fff; color: var(--c-secondary); font-family: inherit;
        }
        .mini-btn:hover { background: var(--bg-2); color: var(--c-primary); }
        .fld-wide { grid-column: span 2; }

        /* Status segmented control */
        .seg { display: inline-flex; border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); border-radius: var(--r-btn); overflow: hidden; }
        .seg button {
            font-family: inherit; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; padding: 6px 12px;
            border: 0; background: #fff; color: var(--c-secondary); cursor: pointer;
        }
        .seg button + button { border-left: 1px solid var(--border-strong); }
        .seg button.on { background: var(--fb-blue); color: #fff; }

        /* ── DEFAULT-RULE BANNER ─────────────────────────────── */
        .rule-banner {
            display: flex; align-items: flex-start; gap: 8px; flex-wrap: wrap;
            margin: 8px 0 0; padding: 8px 10px; border-radius: var(--r-btn);
            font-size: 12px; line-height: 1.45;
        }
        .rule-banner.hidden { display: none; }
        .rule-banner.ok   { background: var(--tint-blue); color: #14425c; border: 1px solid #b9d8ec; }
        .rule-banner.warn { background: var(--acc-orange-bg); color: var(--acc-orange-con); border: 1px solid #ecd2b8; }
        .rule-banner b { font-weight: 700; }
        .rule-banner .lnk { color: var(--link); cursor: pointer; text-decoration: underline; font-weight: 600; }
        .rule-banner .lnk:hover { color: var(--link-hover); }

        /* ── LINE GRID ────────────────────────────────────────
           A CSS grid rather than a <table>: a Note row has to span the data
           columns cleanly, and the zero-height insert band between rows is
           trivial in grid and ugly in a table. */
        /* Grows to fill a tall window, but never collapses to nothing on a
           short one — below this the whole shell scrolls instead. */
        .grid-card { flex: 1 1 auto; display: flex; flex-direction: column; min-height: 280px; overflow: hidden; }
        .grid-scroll { flex: 1; overflow: auto; min-height: 0; }

        /* grid-template-columns and min-width are written by applyGridTemplate()
           from the live column model — the widths are draggable and the order
           is rearrangeable, so they cannot live in the stylesheet. A trailing
           minmax(0,1fr) spacer track absorbs any leftover width. */
        .so-grid { display: grid; }
        .so-row { display: contents; }
        .so-grid > .c {
            padding: 4px 6px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--bg-3);
            display: flex; align-items: center; min-width: 0; min-height: 34px;
        }
        .so-grid > .c.num { justify-content: flex-end; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
        .so-grid > .c.ctr { justify-content: center; text-align: center; }
        .so-grid > .c.ctr .cell-ro,
        .so-grid > .c.ctr .taxcode { width: 100%; text-align: center; }

        /* A hairline between columns. Narrow headings like UOM and Tax Code
           otherwise run together and it stops being obvious which heading
           belongs to which column. Light on the navy header, barely there in
           the body — enough to guide the eye down a column of figures without
           turning the grid into graph paper. */
        .so-grid > .hd { border-right: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.16); }
        .so-grid > .c  { border-right: 1px solid rgba(16,16,16,.045); }
        .so-grid > .hd {
            position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 3;
            background: var(--menu-bg); color: #fff;
            font-size: 10.5px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: .04em; text-transform: uppercase;
            padding: 8px 6px; border-bottom: 0; min-height: 0;
            /* the resize grip is absolutely positioned against this */
            position: -webkit-sticky; position: sticky;
        }
        .so-grid > .hd.num { justify-content: flex-end; }
        .so-grid > .hd.ctr { justify-content: center; text-align: center; }
        .so-grid > .hd.movable { cursor: grab; }
        .so-grid > .hd.movable:active { cursor: grabbing; }
        .so-grid > .hd:hover { background: #164A5F; }
        .so-grid > .hd.col-drag-over { box-shadow: inset 3px 0 0 var(--fb-blue-hover); }
        .so-grid > .hd.col-drag-over-r { box-shadow: inset -3px 0 0 var(--fb-blue-hover); }
        .so-grid > .hd.dragging { opacity: .45; }

        /* Resize grip on the right edge of a header cell. The header is
           position:sticky, which is also a containing block, so absolute
           positioning inside it lands where it should. */
        .col-rz {
            position: absolute; right: 0; top: 0; width: 7px; height: 100%;
            cursor: col-resize; user-select: none; z-index: 4;
        }
        .col-rz:hover, .col-rz.active { background: rgba(255,255,255,.4); }
        body.col-resizing { cursor: col-resize; user-select: none; }

        /* Row drop indicator — the whole row is a drop target, not just the
           thin band between rows, so a drag can land anywhere sensible. */
        .so-grid > .c.drop-before { box-shadow: inset 0 2px 0 var(--fb-blue); }
        .so-grid > .c.drop-after  { box-shadow: inset 0 -2px 0 var(--fb-blue); }
        .so-grid > .c.row-dragging { opacity: .4; }

        /* Row hover — every cell of the hovered row tints together. There is
           no row element to hang :hover on in a display:contents grid, so JS
           stamps .hov on the cells. */
        .so-grid > .c.hov { background: var(--tint-blue); }
        .so-grid > .c.rowsel { background: var(--tint-blue-2); }

        .cell-in {
            font-family: inherit; font-size: 12.5px; color: var(--c-primary);
            border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 4px; background: transparent;
            padding: 4px 5px; width: 100%; min-width: 0;
        }
        .cell-in:hover { border-color: var(--border-strong); background: #fff; }
        .cell-in:focus { outline: none; border-color: var(--fb-blue); background: #fff; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(45,156,219,.18); }
        /* Never type=number in a grid cell — the spinner arrows sit on top of
           the digits at this width. */
        .cell-in.n { text-align: right; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
        .cell-ro { font-size: 12.5px; color: var(--c-secondary); overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; }
        .cell-ro.n { text-align: right; width: 100%; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: var(--c-primary); }

        /* The unit price turns Fishbowl blue the moment it stops being the
           product's list price — the at-a-glance confirmation that a discount
           actually landed on the line. */
        .cell-in.moved, .cell-ro.moved { color: var(--fb-blue-accent); font-weight: 600; }
        .disc { font-size: 11.5px; font-weight: 700; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
        .disc.off  { color: var(--fb-success); }
        .disc.up   { color: var(--acc-orange-con); }
        .disc.free { color: var(--fb-negative); }
        .disc.zero { color: var(--c-tertiary); font-weight: 400; }
        .taxcode { font-size: 11px; color: var(--c-secondary); }
        .taxcode.none { color: var(--c-tertiary); font-style: italic; }
        .cfval {
            font-size: 11.5px; color: var(--acc-purple-con); font-weight: 600;
            overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; width: 100%;
        }
        .cfval.none { color: var(--c-tertiary); font-style: italic; font-weight: 400; }

        .drag-h { cursor: grab; color: var(--bg-4); font-size: 12px; line-height: 1; user-select: none; }
        .drag-h:hover { color: var(--c-tertiary); }
        .row-x {
            border: 0; background: transparent; color: var(--bg-4); cursor: pointer;
            font-size: 15px; line-height: 1; padding: 2px 4px; border-radius: 4px;
        }
        .row-x:hover { color: var(--fb-negative); background: #fbe9ec; }

        /* Pricing-rule cell */
        .rule-btn {
            font-family: inherit; font-size: 12px; text-align: left;
            border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 4px; background: transparent;
            padding: 4px 6px; width: 100%; cursor: pointer; color: var(--c-primary);
            display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; min-width: 0;
        }
        .rule-btn:hover { border-color: var(--border-strong); background: #fff; }
        .rule-btn:focus { outline: none; border-color: var(--fb-blue); background: #fff; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(45,156,219,.18); }
        .rule-btn .nm { flex: 1; min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; }
        .rule-btn .nm.none { color: var(--c-tertiary); font-style: italic; }
        .rule-btn .nm.gone { text-decoration: line-through; color: var(--acc-orange-con); }
        .chip {
            font-size: 9px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: .04em; text-transform: uppercase;
            padding: 1px 5px; border-radius: var(--r-pill); flex-shrink: 0;
        }
        .chip.auto { background: var(--tint-blue-2); color: #14425c; }
        .chip.off  { background: var(--acc-purple-bg); color: var(--acc-purple-con); }
        .chip.man  { background: var(--acc-yellow-bg); color: var(--acc-yellow-con); }
        .chip.ne   { background: var(--acc-orange-bg); color: var(--acc-orange-con); }

        /* Note rows */
        /* 3 / -3 = from just after the pinned # column to just before the
           pinned actions column, whatever the middle columns have been
           rearranged into. */
        .so-grid > .c.note-c {
            grid-column: 3 / -3; background: #fcfcfa; align-items: flex-start; padding-top: 6px;
        }
        .so-grid > .c.new-band { grid-column: 3 / -3; }
        .so-grid > .c.note-g { background: #fcfcfa; }
        .note-in {
            font-family: inherit; font-size: 12.5px; font-style: italic; color: var(--c-secondary);
            border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 4px; background: transparent;
            padding: 3px 5px; width: 100%; resize: none; overflow: hidden; line-height: 1.4;
        }
        .note-in:hover { border-color: var(--border-strong); background: #fff; }
        .note-in:focus { outline: none; border-color: var(--fb-blue); background: #fff; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(45,156,219,.18); }
        .note-glyph { font-size: 11px; color: var(--c-tertiary); }

        /* ── INSERT BAND ──────────────────────────────────────
           Always present at a fixed 7px so revealing the "+" never shifts
           anything below it — the failure that makes most inline-insert
           affordances feel broken. */
        .gap { grid-column: 1 / -1; position: relative; height: 7px; }
        .gap::before {
            content: ''; position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; top: 3px; height: 2px;
            background: var(--fb-blue); opacity: 0; transition: opacity .12s;
        }
        .gap:hover::before, .gap.act::before { opacity: .38; }
        .gap-btn {
            position: absolute; left: 6px; top: -6px;
            width: 19px; height: 19px; border-radius: 50%;
            border: 1px solid var(--fb-blue); background: #fff; color: var(--fb-blue);
            font-size: 14px; line-height: 1; cursor: pointer; padding: 0;
            display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
            opacity: 0; transition: opacity .12s;
        }
        .gap:hover .gap-btn, .gap-btn:focus-visible { opacity: 1; }
        .gap-btn:hover { background: var(--fb-blue); color: #fff; }

        .empty-note { grid-column: 1 / -1; padding: 26px 12px; text-align: center; color: var(--c-tertiary); font-size: 12.5px; }

        /* The blank last row of the grid, where the next product is picked.
           Kept inside the grid rather than lifted into a bar above it, so a
           line is entered where it appears. */
        .so-grid > .c.new-c { background: #fafcfe; }
        .entry-hint { font-size: 11px; color: var(--c-tertiary); white-space: nowrap; }

        /* ── ADDRESS PANELS ───────────────────────────────────
           Blue-headed Bill To / Ship To cards, as the client draws them. The
           picker lives in the header bar so the address itself stays legible. */
        .addr-panel { border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 6px; overflow: hidden; background: #fff; }
        .addr-head {
            background: var(--fb-blue); color: #fff; padding: 4px 8px;
            display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px;
            font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: .02em;
        }
        .addr-head select {
            margin-left: auto; max-width: 62%; font-family: inherit; font-size: 11px;
            padding: 2px 4px; border: 0; border-radius: 4px; background: rgba(255,255,255,.92); color: var(--c-primary);
        }
        .addr-body {
            padding: 6px 9px; font-size: 12px; line-height: 1.45;
            color: var(--c-primary); min-height: 68px; white-space: pre-line;
        }
        .addr-body.empty { color: var(--c-tertiary); font-style: italic; }

        /* ── TYPEAHEAD ───────────────────────────────────────── */
        .ta-pop, .rule-pop {
            position: fixed; z-index: 1200; background: #fff;
            border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); border-radius: 8px;
            box-shadow: var(--sh3); overflow: hidden; display: none;
            flex-direction: column; max-height: 340px;
        }
        .ta-pop.open, .rule-pop.open { display: flex; }
        .ta-list, .rule-list { overflow-y: auto; flex: 1; }
        .ta-item {
            padding: 6px 10px; cursor: pointer; font-size: 12.5px;
            display: flex; gap: 8px; align-items: baseline; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--bg-2);
        }
        .ta-item:last-child { border-bottom: 0; }
        .ta-item.hl, .ta-item:hover { background: var(--tint-blue); }
        .ta-item .pn { font-weight: 700; color: var(--link); flex-shrink: 0; }
        .ta-item .pd { color: var(--c-secondary); flex: 1; min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; }
        .ta-item .pp { color: var(--c-primary); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; flex-shrink: 0; }
        .ta-empty { padding: 12px; text-align: center; color: var(--c-tertiary); font-style: italic; font-size: 12px; }

        /* ── COLUMN PICKER ────────────────────────── */
        .col-pop {
            position: fixed; z-index: 1200; width: 240px; background: #fff;
            border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); border-radius: 8px;
            box-shadow: var(--sh3); overflow: hidden; display: none; flex-direction: column;
        }
        .col-pop.open { display: flex; }
        .col-pop-head {
            padding: 7px 10px; background: var(--bg-2); color: var(--c-secondary);
            font-size: 9.5px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: .05em; text-transform: uppercase;
        }
        .col-list { max-height: 340px; overflow-y: auto; padding: 4px 0; }
        .col-row {
            display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 5px 10px;
            font-size: 12.5px; color: var(--c-primary); cursor: pointer;
        }
        .col-row:hover { background: var(--tint-blue); }
        .col-row.req { cursor: default; color: var(--c-tertiary); }
        .col-row.req:hover { background: transparent; }
        .col-row span { flex: 1; min-width: 0; }
        .col-req {
            flex: 0 0 auto; font-size: 9px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase;
            letter-spacing: .04em; color: var(--c-tertiary);
        }

        /* ── RULE POPOVER ────────────────────────────────────── */
        .rule-pop { width: 420px; }
        .rule-search { padding: 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--bg-3); }
        .rule-search input {
            width: 100%; font-family: inherit; font-size: 12.5px; padding: 6px 8px;
            border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); border-radius: var(--r-btn);
        }
        .rule-search input:focus { outline: none; border-color: var(--fb-blue); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(45,156,219,.15); }
        .rule-grp {
            padding: 5px 10px; background: var(--bg-2); color: var(--c-secondary);
            font-size: 9.5px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: .05em; text-transform: uppercase;
            position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 1;
        }
        .rule-item {
            padding: 6px 10px; cursor: pointer; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--bg-2);
            display: flex; gap: 8px; align-items: center;
        }
        .rule-item:hover, .rule-item.hl { background: var(--tint-blue); }
        .rule-item.dis { opacity: .55; cursor: not-allowed; }
        .rule-item.dis:hover { background: transparent; }
        .rule-item.sel { background: var(--tint-blue-2); }
        .rule-item .ri-main { flex: 1; min-width: 0; }
        .rule-item .ri-nm { font-size: 12.5px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--c-primary); overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; }
        .rule-item .ri-sub { font-size: 11px; color: var(--c-tertiary); overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; }
        .rule-item .ri-px { font-size: 12.5px; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; text-align: right; flex-shrink: 0; }
        .rule-item .ri-dl { font-size: 10px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--fb-success); }
        .rule-foot { padding: 6px 10px; border-top: 1px solid var(--bg-3); display: flex; gap: 8px; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; }
        .rule-foot .lnk { font-size: 11.5px; color: var(--link); cursor: pointer; font-weight: 600; }

        /* ── TOTALS BAR ──────────────────────────────────────── */
        .totals {
            display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 22px; flex-wrap: wrap;
            padding: 9px 14px; border-top: 1px solid var(--border); background: var(--bg-2);

<script>
// ============================================================================
//  RUNTIME GUARD
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
//  This screen both reads (runQuery) and WRITES (runRestApiAsync) — outside
//  Fishbowl neither exists, and a half-working form that silently can't save
//  is worse than an honest refusal.
// ============================================================================
const HAS_QUERY = (typeof runQueryAsync === 'function' || typeof runQuery === 'function');
const HAS_REST  = (typeof runRestApiAsync === 'function');

if (!HAS_QUERY) {
    document.body.innerHTML =
        '<div style="padding:40px;font-family:sans-serif;color:#506872;max-width:620px;">' +
        '<h2 style="color:#101010;">Not running inside Fishbowl</h2>' +
        '<p>This screen reads products, customers and pricing rules through the Fishbowl ' +
        'BI query bridge and creates sales orders through the Fishbowl REST API. Open it ' +
        'from the Fishbowl client.</p></div>';
    throw new Error('Fishbowl query bridge unavailable');
}

// ============================================================================
//  SETTINGS
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
//  Nothing about one client's rule naming belongs in the code — the note
//  matcher is entirely configuration, so another install points it somewhere
//  else without a code change.
// ============================================================================
const DEFAULTS = {
    v: 1,
    ruleCfName: 'Pricing Rule',
    manualOverrideCfValue: '',
    defaultRuleSource: 'note',          // note | cf | note-then-cf | off
    defaultRuleCfName: '',
    // Pulls a rule-shaped phrase ("CP Volume Discount 15%") out of a longer
    // sentence. The class carries NO full stop on purpose: with one, a match
    // starts mid-sentence and swallows the preceding clause, e.g.
    // "day terms. CP Volume Discount 15%", which then equals no rule at all.
    defaultRulePattern: '([A-Za-z][A-Za-z &/-]*?\\s*\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?\\s*%)',
    // Operator shorthand, one per line: "PROF = Professional". Expanded
    // before a note is matched, for shorthand the letter-matching can't reach.
    defaultRuleAliases: '',
    defaultRuleApplyToNewLines: true,
    defaultRuleRequireNumericMatch: true,
    defaultStatusId: 10,
    moduleOpt: 'low',                   // which price wins when rules tie
    // Column widths + order for the line grid, written by the resize and
    // reorder handlers. null = the shipped layout.
    gridCols: null,
    debug: false,
};

try {
    FBLib.Settings.init({
        masterStorage: 'userProperties',   // shared admin defaults via userproperties, not report data (which needs a SAVED report — see FBLib.SharedData)
        userKey:   'cdx.bi.baborSoEntry.user.v1',
        masterKey: 'cdx.bi.baborSoEntry.master.v1',
        defaults:  DEFAULTS,
        propFallback: { debug: { name: 'BI_SHOW_DEBUG', dflt: 'false', parse: v => (v === 'true' || v === true) } },
    });
} catch (e) { console.warn('FBLib.Settings.init failed:', e); }

function pref(k) {
    try { const v = FBLib.Settings.resolve(k); return v === undefined ? DEFAULTS[k] : v; }
    catch (_) { return DEFAULTS[k]; }
}

let DEBUG = !!pref('debug');

// ============================================================================
//  SMALL HELPERS
// ============================================================================
const C = (typeof FBLib !== 'undefined' && FBLib.Common) ? FBLib.Common : null;

// Money always carries the HOME COMPANY's symbol and locale, not a hardcoded
// dollar — fb-lib resolves those from Fishbowl's own currencyLocale(). The
// fallback path asks for the same thing rather than assuming US dollars.
let _cur = null;
function curr() {
    if (_cur) return _cur;
    try { _cur = (typeof currencyLocale === 'function') ? currencyLocale() : null; } catch (_) { _cur = null; }
    if (!_cur || typeof _cur !== 'object') _cur = {};
    if (!_cur.locale) _cur.locale = 'en-US';
    if (!_cur.symbol) _cur.symbol = '$';
    return _cur;
}
function fmtMoney(v) {
    if (C && C.formatMoney) return C.formatMoney(v);
    const n = parseFloat(v); if (isNaN(n)) return '';
    const c = curr();
    return (n < 0 ? '-' : '') + c.symbol +
        Math.abs(n).toLocaleString(c.locale, { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 });
}
function fmtQty(v) {
    if (C && C.formatQty) return C.formatQty(v);
    const n = parseFloat(v); if (isNaN(n)) return '';
    return n % 1 === 0 ? String(Math.round(n)) : String(+n.toFixed(4));
}
function escSQL(s) {
    if (C && C.escSQL) return C.escSQL(s);
    return String(s == null ? '' : s).replace(/'/g, "''");
}
function escHtml(s) {
    return String(s == null ? '' : s)
        .replace(/&/g, '&').replace(/</g, '<').replace(/>/g, '>')
        .replace(/"/g, '"').replace(/'/g, ''');
}
function intOf(v) {
    if (v == null) return null;
    const n = typeof v === 'number' ? v : parseInt(v, 10);
    return isNaN(n) ? null : n;
}
function numOf(v) { const n = parseFloat(v); return isNaN(n) ? null : n; }
function roundCents(n) { return Math.round((parseFloat(n) || 0) * 100) / 100; }

// bit(1) reaches JS as 0/1, true/false, '1'/'0' or a base64 byte depending on
// the driver path. Accept the union.
function bitTrue(v) {
    if (v === 1 || v === true || v === '1') return true;
    if (typeof v === 'object' && v && v[0] === 1) return true;
    if (typeof v === 'string' && (v === 'AQ==' || v === 'true')) return true;
    return false;
}

function dbg(msg, kind) {
    if (!DEBUG) return;
    try { C.debugLog(msg, kind || 'info'); } catch (_) { console.log('[so-entry]', msg); }
}

function setStatusLine(t) { document.getElementById('statusLine').textContent = t; }

function toast(msg, kind, ms) {
    const box = document.getElementById('toastBox');
    const el = document.createElement('div');
    el.className = 'toast ' + (kind || 'info');
    const icon = kind === 'success' ? '✓' : kind === 'error' ? '✕' : kind === 'warn' ? '⚠' : 'ℹ';
    el.innerHTML = '<span class="toast-icon">' + icon + '</span>' +
                   '<span class="toast-msg">' + escHtml(msg) + '</span>' +
                   '<button class="toast-x" type="button">×</button>';
    el.querySelector('.toast-x').addEventListener('click', () => el.remove());
    box.appendChild(el);
    const life = ms || (kind === 'error' ? 12000 : 4500);

// Query bridge. runQueryAsync already returns parsed rows with lowercased
// keys; runQuery returns a JSON string and may hand back a bare object when
// there is exactly one row.
async function qp(sql) {
    if (typeof runQueryAsync === 'function') {
        const r = await runQueryAsync(sql);
        return Array.isArray(r) ? r : (r ? [r] : []);
    }
    const raw = runQuery(sql);
    if (!raw) return [];
    let r; try { r = JSON.parse(raw); } catch (_) { return []; }
    if (r == null) return [];
    return Array.isArray(r) ? r : [r];
}

async function loadCustomers() {
    const cfName = String(pref('defaultRuleCfName') || '').trim();
    // The note is the prompt the operator reads today ("Volume Discount 20%"),
    // so it is also what the default-rule matcher reads. A custom field is
    // offered as an alternative source for installs that keep it elsewhere.
    const cfSel = cfName
        ? `CustomFieldByName(cu.customFields, '${escSQL(cfName)}') AS ruleprompt`
        : `'' AS ruleprompt`;
    const rows = await qp(`
        SELECT cu.id, cu.number, cu.name, cu.accountId, cu.note,
               cu.parentId, par.name AS parentname,
               cu.taxRateId, cu.defaultSalesmanId, cu.defaultCarrierId,
               ${cfSel},
               tr.name AS taxratename,
               sm.userName AS salesmanname
        FROM customer cu
        LEFT JOIN customer par ON par.id = cu.parentId
        LEFT JOIN taxrate tr ON tr.id = cu.taxRateId
        LEFT JOIN sysuser sm ON sm.id = cu.defaultSalesmanId
        WHERE cu.activeFlag = 1
        ORDER BY cu.name
        LIMIT 5000
    `);
    const nameById = new Map();
    rows.forEach(r => { const i = intOf(r.id); if (i != null) nameById.set(i, String(r.name || '')); });

    _customers = rows.map(r => ({
        id: intOf(r.id), num: r.number, name: String(r.name || ''),
        parentId: intOf(r.parentid),
        parentName: (r.parentid != null ? nameById.get(intOf(r.parentid)) : null) || r.parentname || '',
        accountId: intOf(r.accountid),
        note: r.note != null ? String(r.note) : '',
        rulePrompt: r.ruleprompt != null ? String(r.ruleprompt) : '',
        taxRateId: intOf(r.taxrateid), taxRateName: r.taxratename || '',
        salesmanId: intOf(r.defaultsalesmanid), salesmanName: r.salesmanname || '',
        carrierId: intOf(r.defaultcarrierid),
    }));

    // Cluster sub-customers under their parent, at the PARENT's alphabetical
    // position. Picking the wrong record here means the wrong default rule, so
    // the label has to make the relationship obvious.
    _customers.sort((a, b) => {
        const ka = a.parentName || a.name, kb = b.parentName || b.name;
        const r = ka.localeCompare(kb, undefined, { sensitivity: 'base', numeric: true });
        if (r !== 0) return r;
        const ac = a.parentName ? 1 : 0, bc = b.parentName ? 1 : 0;
        if (ac !== bc) return ac - bc;
        return a.name.localeCompare(b.name, undefined, { sensitivity: 'base', numeric: true });
    });

    // Only append the customer number where the FULL label is still ambiguous
    // — "Parent > Child" already distinguishes a same-named sub-customer.
    const counts = new Map();
    _customers.forEach(c => { const l = baseLabel(c); counts.set(l, (counts.get(l) || 0) + 1); });
    const dupes = new Set([...counts.entries()].filter(([, n]) => n > 1).map(([l]) => l));
    _customers.forEach(c => { c.label = baseLabel(c) + (dupes.has(baseLabel(c)) ? '  (#' + (c.num || c.id) + ')' : ''); });

    const sel = document.getElementById('fCustomer');
    sel.innerHTML = '<option value="">— Select a customer —</option>' +
        _customers.map(c => '<option value="' + c.id + '">' + escHtml(c.label) + '</option>').join('');
}
function baseLabel(c) { return c.parentName ? c.parentName + ' > ' + c.name : c.name; }

async function loadProducts() {
    // producttotree is many-to-many, so GROUP_CONCAT collapses the tree
    // assignments instead of multiplying the product into duplicate rows.
    const rows = await qp(`
        SELECT product.id, product.num, product.description, product.price,
               product.sku, product.upc, product.taxableFlag, product.partId,
               product.taxId, product.kitFlag, product.defaultSoItemType,
               GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT producttree.id) AS treeids,
               uom.code AS uomcode
        FROM product
        LEFT JOIN producttotree ON product.id = producttotree.productId
        LEFT JOIN producttree ON producttotree.productTreeId = producttree.id
        LEFT JOIN uom ON product.uomId = uom.id
        WHERE product.id > 0 AND product.activeFlag = 1
        GROUP BY product.id, product.num, product.description, product.price,
                 product.sku, product.upc, product.taxableFlag, product.partId,
                 product.taxId, product.kitFlag, product.defaultSoItemType, uom.code
        ORDER BY product.num

    `);

        price: numOf(r.price) || 0,
        sku: r.sku || '', upc: r.upc || '',

// Narrow the active rules to those in scope for this customer. A failed group
// lookup fails CLOSED — charging another group's pricing is worse than falling
// back to customer-specific rules and the product price.
async function loadRulesForCustomer(customer) {
    if (!customer) { _activeRules = []; return; }
    const all = [..._allRulesById.values()];
    let groupIds = new Set();
    if (customer.accountId != null) {
        try {
            const g = await qp(`SELECT groupId AS groupid FROM accountgrouprelation WHERE accountId = ${customer.accountId}`);
            groupIds = new Set(g.map(r => intOf(r.groupid)).filter(n => n != null));
        } catch (e) {
            console.warn('Customer group lookup failed — group-scoped rules disabled:', e);
            dbg('Customer group lookup failed; group rules disabled for this customer', 'warn');
        }
    }
    // customerincltype: 1 All · 2 Customer · 3 Customer Group
    _activeRules = all.filter(r => {
        const t = intOf(r.customerincltypeid);
        if (t === 1) return true;
        if (t === 2) return intOf(r.customerinclid) === customer.id;
        if (t === 3) return groupIds.has(intOf(r.customerinclid));
        return false;
    });
    dbg('Customer "' + customer.name + '": ' + _activeRules.length + ' of ' + all.length +
        ' rules in scope; groups [' + ([...groupIds].join(', ') || 'none') + ']');
    if (_activeRules.some(ruleUsesCostBase)) await loadPartCosts();

// One-shot cache of the cost columns cost-based rules resolve against.
// partcost has at most one row per part; vendorparts has one per vendor × UOM,
// so the default vendor's cost and the newest cost are kept separately.
async function loadPartCosts() {
    if (_partCostsLoaded) return;
    _partCostsLoaded = true;
    try {
        const [costRows, vpRows] = await Promise.all([
            qp(`SELECT part.id AS partid, part.stdCost AS stdcost, partcost.avgCost AS avgcost
                FROM part LEFT JOIN partcost ON partcost.partId = part.id`),
            qp(`SELECT partId AS partid, lastCost AS lastcost, defaultFlag AS defaultflag, lastDate AS lastdate
                FROM vendorparts WHERE lastCost IS NOT NULL`),
        ]);
        costRows.forEach(r => {
            const pid = intOf(r.partid); if (pid == null) return;
            _partCosts.set(pid, { avg: numOf(r.avgcost), std: numOf(r.stdcost), vendor: null, last: null, _d: '' });
        });
        vpRows.forEach(r => {
            const pid = intOf(r.partid); if (pid == null) return;
            let e = _partCosts.get(pid);
            if (!e) { e = { avg: null, std: null, vendor: null, last: null, _d: '' }; _partCosts.set(pid, e); }
            const cost = numOf(r.lastcost); if (cost == null) return;
            if (bitTrue(r.defaultflag) && e.vendor == null) e.vendor = cost;
            const d = r.lastdate ? String(r.lastdate) : '';
            if (e.last == null || d > e._d) { e.last = cost; e._d = d; }
        });
        dbg('Cached cost bases for ' + _partCosts.size + ' parts');
    } catch (e) {
        _partCostsLoaded = false;   // allow a retry on the next customer change
        console.warn('loadPartCosts failed:', e);
    }
}

//  PRICING — PRIMARY SOURCE: GET /api/products/:id/best-price
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
//  This returns Fishbowl's OWN candidate rules for the product, each with the
//  price Fishbowl's own engine computes and a `valid` flag marking the one it
//  would auto-apply. Entries marked invalid still carry a price, which is
//  exactly what a manual application of a sample/BDF rule needs.
//
//  Its query parameters are not documented anywhere authoritative — the names
//  below come from the in-house API tool — so the spelling is PROBED once per
//  session against a real product and never persisted. A cached shape would
//  outlive a server upgrade; one wasted round trip per session is cheaper.
// ============================================================================
const BP_PARAM_SHAPES = [
    ['customerId', 'quantity', 'includePricingRules'],
    ['customerId', 'qty',      'includePricingRules'],
    ['customerId', 'quantity', 'includeRules'],
    ['customerId', 'quantity', null],
];
let _bpShape = null;            // null = unprobed · false = unusable · array = winning shape
let _bpProbing = null;
const _bpCache = new Map();     // key -> {best, rules[]}
const _bpInflight = new Map();

function bpKey(productId, qty, customerId) { return productId + '|' + qty + '|' + customerId; }

async function bpCall(productId, qty, customerId, shape) {
    const params = [[shape[0], String(customerId)], [shape[1], String(qty)]];
    if (shape[2]) params.push([shape[2], 'true']);
    return await runRestApiAsync({
        method: 'GET',
        path: '/api/products/' + productId + '/best-price',
        queryParameters: params,
    });
}

async function probeBestPrice(productId, qty, customerId) {
    if (_bpShape !== null) return _bpShape;
    if (_bpProbing) return await _bpProbing;
    _bpProbing = (async () => {
        if (!HAS_REST) { _bpShape = false; return false; }
        for (const shape of BP_PARAM_SHAPES) {
            try {
                const r = await bpCall(productId, qty, customerId, shape);
                const rules = r && (r.pricingRules || r.pricingrules);
                if (Array.isArray(rules) && rules.length) {
                    _bpShape = shape;
                    dbg('best-price parameter shape resolved: ' + JSON.stringify(shape));
                    return shape;
                }
                dbg('best-price shape ' + JSON.stringify(shape) + ' answered without a rule list', 'warn');
            } catch (e) {
                dbg('best-price shape ' + JSON.stringify(shape) + ' failed: ' + (e && e.message || e), 'warn');
            }
        }
        _bpShape = false;
        dbg('best-price is unusable on this server — the picker will price rules locally instead.', 'warn');
        return false;
    })();
    const out = await _bpProbing;
    _bpProbing = null;
    return out;
}

// Server-side candidates for one line. Returns [] when the endpoint can't
// answer, which is the signal to fall back to the local engine.
async function serverCandidates(product, qty, customerId) {
    if (!HAS_REST || !product || customerId == null) return [];
    const key = bpKey(product.id, qty, customerId);
    if (_bpCache.has(key)) return _bpCache.get(key).rules;
    if (_bpInflight.has(key)) { const r = await _bpInflight.get(key); return r.rules; }

    const p = (async () => {
        const shape = await probeBestPrice(product.id, qty, customerId);
        if (!shape) return { best: null, rules: [] };
        let resp;
        try { resp = await bpCall(product.id, qty, customerId, shape); }
        catch (e) { dbg('best-price failed for ' + product.num + ': ' + (e && e.message || e), 'warn'); return { best: null, rules: [] }; }
        const raw = (resp && (resp.pricingRules || resp.pricingrules)) || [];
        const rules = raw.map(r => ({
            id: intOf(r.id),
            name: String(r.name || ''),
            description: r.description || '',
            unitPrice: numOf(r.unitPrice != null ? r.unitPrice : r.unitprice),
            valid: r.valid === true || r.valid === 'true',
            source: 'server',
        })).filter(r => r.id != null && r.unitPrice != null);
        return { best: numOf(resp && (resp.bestUnitPrice || resp.bestunitprice)), rules };
    })();

    _bpInflight.set(key, p);
    let out;
    try { out = await p; } finally { _bpInflight.delete(key); }
    _bpCache.set(key, out);
    return out.rules;
}

// ============================================================================
//  PRICING — LOCAL ENGINE (fallback + off-list pricing)
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
//  Ported from QuickOrder.htm. Enum mappings are CALIBRATED against the live
//  lookup tables (patype, pabaseamounttype, customerincltype), not guessed:
//    patype:            1 Markdown · 2 Markup · 3 Margin · 4 Percent ·
//                       5 Amount · 6 Set price
//    pabaseamounttype:  1 Average Cost · 2 Default Vendor's Cost ·
//                       3 Last Cost · 4 List Price · 5 Product Price ·
//                       6 Standard Cost · 7 Customer Last Price ·
//                       8 Last Manufactured Cost
//    customerincltype:  1 All · 2 Customer · 3 Customer Group
// ============================================================================
function ruleIsTier2(r) { return bitTrue(r.istier2); }

// productInclTypeId: 1 = all · 2 = a specific product · 3 = a product tree
function productMatchesRule(product, r) {
    const t = intOf(r.productincltypeid), inclId = intOf(r.productinclid);
    if (t === 1) return true;
    if (t === 2) return inclId === product.id;
    if (t === 3) return inclId != null && (product.treeIds || []).includes(inclId);
    return false;
}

// qtyApplies is frequently false on rules that still carry a meaningful
// bracket, so the bracket is enforced whenever qtyMin/qtyMax is populated.
function qtyMatchesRule(qty, r) {
    const mn = numOf(r.qtymin), mx = numOf(r.qtymax);
    const hasMin = mn != null && mn > 0, hasMax = mx != null && mx > 0;
    if (!hasMin && !hasMax) return true;
    if (hasMin && qty < mn) return false;
    if (hasMax && qty > mx) return false;
    return true;
}

// Lower rank wins: 1 Customer · 2 Customer Group · 3 Fixed · 4 Other.
function ruleTypeRank(r) {
    const ct = intOf(r.customerincltypeid);
    if (ct === 2) return 1;
    if (ct === 3) return 2;
    return adjustmentType(r) === 'fixed_price' ? 3 : 4;
}

function adjustmentType(r) {
    switch (intOf(r.patypeid)) {
        case 1: return 'markdown';
        case 2: return 'markup';
        case 3: return 'margin';
        case 4: return 'percent';
        case 5: return 'amount';
        case 6: return 'fixed_price';
        default: return 'markdown';
    }
}

const PA_BASE_NAMES = {
    1: 'Average Cost', 2: "Default Vendor's Cost", 3: 'Last Cost', 4: 'List Price',
    5: 'Product Price', 6: 'Standard Cost', 7: 'Customer Last Price', 8: 'Last Manufactured Cost',
};
function baseTypeName(r) { return PA_BASE_NAMES[intOf(r.pabaseamounttypeid)] || 'Product Price'; }

function describeRule(r) {
    if (!r) return '';
    const kind = adjustmentType(r);
    const pct = numOf(r.papercent), amt = numOf(r.paamount);
    const pctS = pct == null ? '?' : ((pct * 100) % 1 ? (pct * 100).toFixed(1) : (pct * 100).toFixed(0)) + '%';
    switch (kind) {
        case 'markdown':    return 'Markdown ' + pctS + ' off ' + baseTypeName(r);
        case 'markup':      return 'Markup ' + pctS + ' on ' + baseTypeName(r);
        case 'margin':      return 'Margin ' + pctS + ' on ' + baseTypeName(r);
        case 'percent':     return pctS + ' of ' + baseTypeName(r);
        case 'amount':      return amt == null ? baseTypeName(r) : baseTypeName(r) + (amt < 0 ? ' − ' : ' + ') + fmtMoney(Math.abs(amt));
        case 'fixed_price': return amt == null ? 'Set price' : 'Set price ' + fmtMoney(amt);
        default:            return '';
    }
}

// Returns null when the base can't be resolved (no cost row, the customer has
// never bought the product, List Price referenced from Tier 2) so the rule is
// SKIPPED rather than priced at $0.
function adjustmentBase(r, product, productPrice, listPrice) {
    const b = intOf(r.pabaseamounttypeid);
    const costs = product && product.partId != null ? _partCosts.get(product.partId) : null;
    switch (b) {
        case 1: return costs && costs.avg    != null ? costs.avg    : null;
        case 2: return costs && costs.vendor != null ? costs.vendor : null;
        case 3: return costs && costs.last   != null ? costs.last   : null;
        case 4: return listPrice != null ? listPrice : null;
        case 6: return costs && costs.std    != null ? costs.std    : null;
        case 7: { const lp = product ? _customerLastPrice.get(product.id) : null; return lp != null && lp > 0 ? lp : null; }
        case 8: return null;
        case 5:
        default: return productPrice;
    }
}

// paPercent is stored as a DECIMAL FRACTION (0.2 means 20%, 1.0 means 100%),
// so these formulas do NOT divide by 100. paApplies is deliberately ignored —
// it is often false on rules that carry a perfectly usable adjustment.
function applyRuleAdjustment(r, product, productPrice, listPrice) {
    const base = adjustmentBase(r, product, productPrice, listPrice);
    if (base == null) return null;
    const kind = adjustmentType(r);
    const pct = numOf(r.papercent), amt = numOf(r.paamount);
    switch (kind) {
        case 'markdown':    return pct == null ? null : base * (1 - pct);
        case 'markup':      return pct == null ? null : base * (1 + pct);
        case 'margin':      return pct == null ? null : (pct >= 1 ? base : base / (1 - pct));
        case 'percent':     return pct == null ? null : base * pct;
        case 'amount':      return amt == null ? null : Math.max(0, base + amt);
        case 'fixed_price': return amt == null ? null : amt;
        default:            return null;
    }
}

// One tier's competition — only the highest-ranked TYPE present competes.
function competeAtTier(tierRules, product, productPrice, listPrice) {
    if (!tierRules || !tierRules.length) return { winner: null, winnerPrice: null };
    const minRank = Math.min(...tierRules.map(ruleTypeRank));
    const scored = [];
    for (const r of tierRules.filter(x => ruleTypeRank(x) === minRank)) {
        const p = applyRuleAdjustment(r, product, productPrice, listPrice);
        if (p == null || !isFinite(p) || p < 0) continue;
        scored.push({ rule: r, price: p });
    }
    if (!scored.length) return { winner: null, winnerPrice: null };
    let win = scored[0];
    for (const s of scored.slice(1)) {
        if (_moduleOpt === 'high' ? s.price > win.price : s.price < win.price) win = s;
    }
    return { winner: win.rule, winnerPrice: win.price };
}

// Two-stage resolution: Tier 2 produces the list price, Tier 3 competes
// against it to produce the sales price. The Tier 2 winner loses its rule TYPE
// before entering Tier 3, which is why the tiers run independently.
function resolveLocal(product, qty) {
    if (!product) return { price: 0, listPrice: 0, t2: null, t3: null };
    const q = qty > 0 ? qty : 1;
    const applicable = _activeRules.filter(r => productMatchesRule(product, r) && qtyMatchesRule(q, r));
    const t2 = competeAtTier(applicable.filter(ruleIsTier2), product, product.price, null);
    const listPrice = t2.winnerPrice != null ? t2.winnerPrice : product.price;
    const t3 = competeAtTier(applicable.filter(r => !ruleIsTier2(r)), product, product.price, listPrice);
    const salesPrice = t3.winnerPrice != null ? t3.winnerPrice : listPrice;
    return { price: roundCents(salesPrice), listPrice: roundCents(listPrice), t2: t2.winner, t3: t3.winner };
}

// Every rule applicable to this product+qty, priced.
//
// This is NOT competeAtTier's `scored` array: that filters to the winning type
// rank BEFORE scoring, so the rules it discards are only the ones that tied.
// A manually applied rule is by definition one the ladder eliminated, so the
// picker has to see all of them.
function localCandidates(product, qty) {
    const q = qty > 0 ? qty : 1;
    const applicable = _activeRules.filter(r => productMatchesRule(product, r) && qtyMatchesRule(q, r));
    const auto = resolveLocal(product, q);
    const winners = new Set([auto.t2 && intOf(auto.t2.id), auto.t3 && intOf(auto.t3.id)].filter(v => v != null));
    const t2 = competeAtTier(applicable.filter(ruleIsTier2), product, product.price, null);
    const listPrice = t2.winnerPrice != null ? t2.winnerPrice : product.price;
    const out = [];
    for (const r of applicable) {
        const p = applyRuleAdjustment(r, product, product.price, ruleIsTier2(r) ? null : listPrice);
        if (p == null || !isFinite(p) || p < 0) continue;
        out.push({
            id: intOf(r.id), name: String(r.name || ''), description: r.description || '',
            unitPrice: roundCents(p), valid: winners.has(intOf(r.id)), source: 'local',
        });
    }
    return out;
}

// The rule Fishbowl would attach BY ITSELF as a product is added — the same
// two-tier ladder, restricted to rules flagged "apply this rule as products
// are added" (pricingrule.isAutoApply). Every other rule is applied only
// because the operator picked it, and that distinction is what makes an
// automatic attribution safe to RECORD rather than merely display.
//
// Note this is not a port: QuickOrder loads isAutoApply but never gates on
// it. The ladder below is shared; the gate is new.
function autoApplyWinner(product, qty) {
    if (!product) return null;
    const q = qty > 0 ? qty : 1;
    const auto = _activeRules.filter(r => bitTrue(r.isautoapply)
        && productMatchesRule(product, r) && qtyMatchesRule(q, r));
    if (!auto.length) return null;
    const t2 = competeAtTier(auto.filter(ruleIsTier2), product, product.price, null);
    const listPrice = t2.winnerPrice != null ? t2.winnerPrice : product.price;
    const t3 = competeAtTier(auto.filter(r => !ruleIsTier2(r)), product, product.price, listPrice);
    // Tier 3 sets the sales price, so it is the tier that gets attributed.
    return t3.winner || t2.winner || null;
}

// Every OTHER active rule, priced locally, for manual application. Rules whose
// base can't resolve come back priced null and render disabled with a reason,
// rather than silently vanishing.
function offListCandidates(product, qty, excludeIds) {
    const q = qty > 0 ? qty : 1;
    const listPrice = resolveLocal(product, q).listPrice;
    const out = [];
    for (const r of _allRulesById.values()) {
        const id = intOf(r.id);
        if (excludeIds.has(id)) continue;
        const p = applyRuleAdjustment(r, product, product.price, ruleIsTier2(r) ? null : listPrice);
        out.push({
            id, name: String(r.name || ''), description: r.description || '',
            unitPrice: (p == null || !isFinite(p) || p < 0) ? null : roundCents(p),
            valid: false, source: 'offlist',
            blocked: (p == null) ? ('needs ' + baseTypeName(r) + ', which this product has no value for') : null,
        });
    }
    return out.sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name, undefined, { sensitivity: 'base' }));
}

// Build the whole candidate list for a line: server first (authoritative),
// local as the fallback, and off-list always appended.
async function candidatesForLine(line) {
    const product = line.product, qty = line.qty > 0 ? line.qty : 1;
    if (!product) return { inScope: [], offList: [], source: 'none' };

    let inScope = [];
    let source = 'local';
    if (_bpShape !== false && _customer) {
        try { inScope = await serverCandidates(product, qty, _customer.id); } catch (_) { inScope = []; }
        if (inScope.length) source = 'server';
    }
    const local = localCandidates(product, qty);
    if (!inScope.length) {
        inScope = local;
    } else {
        // The server answers with id/name/price but not the adjustment shape,
        // so the local rows supply the "Markdown 20% off Product Price" label
        // and flag any price we disagree with.
        const localById = new Map(local.map(c => [c.id, c]));
        inScope.forEach(c => {
            const l = localById.get(c.id);
            if (l && Math.abs(l.unitPrice - c.unitPrice) >= 0.01) {
                c.mismatch = l.unitPrice;
                dbg('rule ' + c.id + ' "' + c.name + '": server ' + c.unitPrice + ' vs local ' + l.unitPrice, 'warn');
            }
        });
    }
    const seen = new Set(inScope.map(c => c.id));
    return { inScope, offList: offListCandidates(product, qty, seen), source };
}

// ============================================================================
//  DEFAULT RULE FROM THE CUSTOMER'S NOTE
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
//  The operator's prompt today is free text on the customer ("Volume Discount
//  20%"), updated by hand each month. Matching it to a rule is what removes
//  the per-line hunt — but a WRONG default that nobody notices is worse than
//  no default, so every outcome is reported in the banner and every
//  auto-picked cell is visibly marked.
// ============================================================================
function normText(s) {
    return String(s == null ? '' : s).toLowerCase()
        // Replace rather than delete: deleting the hyphen in "30-day" fuses it
        // into the single nonsense token "30day".
        .replace(/[^a-z0-9%.]+/g, ' ')
        // A full stop ENDING a token is sentence punctuation, not part of a
        // rule name. One between digits ("15.5%") is, so it stays.
        .replace(/(^|\s)\.+/g, '$1').replace(/\.+(?=\s|$)/g, '')
        .replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
}
function numTokens(s) { return (String(s).match(/\d+(?:\.\d+)?/g) || []); }

// A note names ONE OR MORE rules, joined by "&", "+", a comma, a semicolon or
// a newline: "PROF 15% & SVC 20%" is two instructions, not one. Each piece is
// matched to a rule separately, and ALL the matches are kept — which one lands
// on a given line is then decided by the rules' own product scopes.
function noteSegments(text) {
    return String(text == null ? '' : text)
        .split(/[\n;&+,]+/)
        .map(x => x.trim())
        .filter(Boolean);
}

// Operator shorthand, expanded before matching: "PROF = Professional", one per
// line in Settings. This is the escape hatch for shorthand the letter-matching
// below can't reach on its own ("BDF = Business Development Fund").
let _aliasCache = null, _aliasSrc = null;
function aliasMap() {
    const src = String(pref('defaultRuleAliases') || '');
    if (_aliasCache && _aliasSrc === src) return _aliasCache;
    const m = new Map();
    src.split(/[\n;]+/).forEach(line => {
        const bits = line.split(/[=:]/);
        if (bits.length < 2) return;
        const from = normText(bits[0]), to = normText(bits.slice(1).join('='));
        if (from && to) m.set(from, to);
    });
    _aliasSrc = src; _aliasCache = m;
    return m;
}
function expandAliases(segN) {
    const m = aliasMap();
    if (!m.size) return segN;
    // Whole-phrase first, then word by word, so both "PROF 15% = Professional
    // 15%" and the simpler "PROF = Professional" work.
    if (m.has(segN)) return m.get(segN);
    return segN.split(' ').map(w => m.get(w) || w).join(' ');
}

// Does this shorthand stand for that word?
//   "prof" -> "professional"  (a plain prefix)
//   "svc"  -> "service"       (letters in order, first letter shared)
// The shared first letter and the length floor are what stop it degenerating
// into "any three letters match almost any word".
function abbrevMatches(short, word) {
    if (!short || !word) return false;
    if (short === word) return true;
    if (short.length < 2 || short.length >= word.length) return false;
    if (short[0] !== word[0]) return false;
    if (word.indexOf(short) === 0) return true;
    let i = 0;
    for (let k = 0; k < word.length; k++) {
        if (word[k] === short[i]) i++;
        if (i === short.length) return true;
    }
    return false;
}

const _isNumTok = t => /^\d/.test(t) || t === '%';

// Match one note segment to a rule by abbreviation. Words must line up from
// the START of the rule name, in order, and any numbers must agree EXACTLY —
// "PROF 15%" must never reach "Professional 20%".
function matchByAbbrev(segN, rules, requireNumeric) {
    const segToks = segN.split(' ').filter(Boolean);
    const segWords = segToks.filter(t => !_isNumTok(t));
    const segNums = numTokens(segN);
    if (!segWords.length) return [];

    const hits = [];
    for (const r of rules) {
        const nameN = normText(r.name);
        const nameToks = nameN.split(' ').filter(Boolean);
        const nameWords = nameToks.filter(t => !_isNumTok(t));
        if (!nameWords.length || segWords.length > nameWords.length) continue;

        if (requireNumeric) {
            const rNums = numTokens(nameN);
            if (rNums.length !== segNums.length) continue;
            if (rNums.some((n, i) => n !== segNums[i])) continue;
        }
        let ok = true, score = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < segWords.length; i++) {
            if (!abbrevMatches(segWords[i], nameWords[i])) { ok = false; break; }
            score += segWords[i].length;
        }
        if (!ok) continue;
        // A shorthand covering the whole name beats one covering half of it.
        hits.push({ rule: r, score: score + (segWords.length === nameWords.length ? 10 : 0) });
    }
    if (!hits.length) return [];
    const best = Math.max(...hits.map(h => h.score));
    return hits.filter(h => h.score === best).map(h => h.rule);
}

// One segment -> one rule, or a reason it could not be resolved.
function matchSegment(segRaw, rules, requireNumeric) {
    const segN0 = normText(segRaw);
    if (!segN0) return null;
    const segN = expandAliases(segN0);
    const alias = segN !== segN0;

    // 1 — the expanded text IS a rule name
    let hit = rules.find(r => normText(r.name) === segN);
    if (hit) return { rule: hit, text: segRaw, kind: alias ? 'alias' : 'exact' };

    // 2 — pull a rule-shaped phrase out of a sentence, then retry
    let pat = null;
    try { pat = new RegExp(pref('defaultRulePattern'), 'i'); } catch (_) {}
    if (pat) {
        const m = segRaw.match(pat);
        if (m && m[1]) {
            const capN = expandAliases(normText(m[1]));
            hit = rules.find(r => normText(r.name) === capN);
            if (hit) return { rule: hit, text: segRaw, kind: 'pattern', capture: m[1] };
        }
    }

    // 3 — abbreviation: "PROF 15%" -> "Professional 15%"
    const abbrev = matchByAbbrev(segN, rules, requireNumeric);
    if (abbrev.length === 1) return { rule: abbrev[0], text: segRaw, kind: 'abbreviation' };
    if (abbrev.length > 1) return { text: segRaw, miss: 'ambiguous', names: abbrev.map(r => r.name) };

    // A bare "SVC" names the right family but not WHICH of them, because the
    // rules differ only by percentage. Saying "no rule resembles it" would be
    // misleading — the operator needs to know the note is short a number.
    if (requireNumeric && !numTokens(segN).length) {
        const loose = matchByAbbrev(segN, rules, false);
        if (loose.length > 1) return { text: segRaw, miss: 'ambiguous', names: loose.map(r => r.name) };
        if (loose.length === 1) return { rule: loose[0], text: segRaw, kind: 'abbreviation' };
    }

    // 4 — every word of the rule name appears somewhere in the segment. The
    // numeric guard matters most here: without it "Volume Discount 20%"
    // happily matches "Volume Discount 25%", which is a silent pricing error.
    const segTokens = new Set(segN.split(' ').filter(Boolean));
    const segNums = numTokens(segN);
    let best = [], bestScore = 0;
    for (const r of rules) {
        const nameN = normText(r.name);
        const toks = nameN.split(' ').filter(Boolean);
        if (!toks.length || !toks.every(t => segTokens.has(t))) continue;
        if (requireNumeric) {
            const rNums = numTokens(nameN);
            if (rNums.length || segNums.length) {
                if (rNums.length !== rNums.filter(n => segNums.includes(n)).length) continue;
                if (!rNums.length) continue;   // the note names a number, the rule doesn't
            }
        }
        if (toks.length > bestScore) { bestScore = toks.length; best = [r]; }
        else if (toks.length === bestScore) best.push(r);
    }
    if (best.length === 1) return { rule: best[0], text: segRaw, kind: 'wording' };
    if (best.length > 1) return { text: segRaw, miss: 'ambiguous', names: best.map(r => r.name) };

    return { text: segRaw, miss: 'none' };
}

// Resolve the customer's note into the SET of rules it names. Nothing is
// applied here: which of them lands on a given line is settled per line, by
// each rule's own product scope and quantity bracket.
function resolveDefaultRules(customer) {
    _defaultRules = []; _defaultRuleMisses = []; _defaultRuleText = '';
    const mode = pref('defaultRuleSource');
    if (!customer || mode === 'off') return;

    let text = '';
    if (mode === 'note') text = customer.note || '';
    else if (mode === 'cf') text = customer.rulePrompt || '';
    else text = (customer.note || '').trim() || (customer.rulePrompt || '');
    _defaultRuleText = String(text || '').trim();
    if (!_defaultRuleText) { _defaultRuleMisses.push({ miss: 'no-text' }); return; }

    const rules = [..._allRulesById.values()];
    const requireNumeric = !!pref('defaultRuleRequireNumericMatch');
    const seen = new Set();

    for (const seg of noteSegments(_defaultRuleText)) {
        const res = matchSegment(seg, rules, requireNumeric);
        if (!res) continue;
        if (res.rule) {
            const id = intOf(res.rule.id);
            if (seen.has(id)) continue;          // the same rule named twice
            seen.add(id);
            _defaultRules.push(res);
        } else {
            // A segment that resolves to nothing is usually just prose
            // ("call before shipping"), so it is only worth reporting when
            // NOTHING in the note resolved. That decision is made in the
            // banner, where the whole picture is visible.
            _defaultRuleMisses.push(res);
        }
    }
    dbg('customer note resolved to ' + _defaultRules.length + ' rule(s): ' +
        (_defaultRules.map(d => d.rule.name).join(', ') || 'none'));
}
